children: The State Bank of India (SBI) plans to significantly expand the size of loans available to small businesses under its digital lending programme, MSME Dream, with the per-borrower limit set to rise from the current Rs 5 crore to as much as Rs 50 crore by March 2027.

The country's largest lender will implement the expansion in phases, with the first increase expected to take the ceiling to Rs 10 crore by November 30. The limit will subsequently be raised to Rs 50 crore across its branch network by March 2027, a senior SBI official told

Launched in December 2023, MSME Dream enables micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to access credit through a digital application and assessment process. SBI has sanctioned loans worth approximately Rs 2.25 lakh crore through the platform since its launch, the official said.
The proposed expansion reflects the bank's assessment of the financing needs of businesses in the MSME segment, which plays a significant role in industrial activity, employment and exports.
"The MSME sector is not merely an economic segment; it is an important pillar of India's industrial development, employment generation, exports, innovation and inclusive growth," the official said.
The bank expects the digital lending model to support larger credit requirements without significantly slowing down the approval process.

Under the MSME Dream programme, borrowers submit relevant business and financial details through a digital platform, which evaluates their creditworthiness using available data and digital footprints.

The system can issue an in-principle loan approval within 30-45 minutes, according to the SBI official. The time taken to disburse credit has also fallen substantially, from around three to four weeks under the earlier process to approximately one week.
The streamlined assessment mechanism uses digital records and other inputs to speed up credit evaluation and reduce the time businesses spend waiting for financing.

SBI has also reported better asset quality in the loans sanctioned through the programme. The gross non-performing asset (NPA) ratio under MSME Dream is below 0.50%, compared with more than 1.50% for its overall MSME loan portfolio, the official said.
The expansion comes against the backdrop of the MSME sector's growing contribution to the Indian economy.
According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, MSMEs account for 31.1% of India's GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing output and 48.58% of total exports.

The sector is also central to the government's Viksit Bharat 2047 ambition. The SBI official said MSMEs and manufacturing would need to expand, improve competitiveness and transform their operations to support India's transition towards a developed economy.

title: SBI plans to raise MSME loan limit 10-fold to Rs 50 crore by March 2027
